themes_detail.label: E-Scooter Proliferation Crisis
themes_detail.summary: E-scooter complaints spiked to 7 this week versus a historical average of 0.6 per week—a 1,020% increase (z-score: 9.16)—suggesting rapid, unregulated deployment or operational chaos in Throgs Neck/Co-op City over the past 2 weeks.
evidence: 7 e-scooter complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,020% spike)
Z-score of 9.16 indicates statistically severe anomaly
Spike is one of the most extreme deviations in the dataset
reporting_angles: Which e-scooter companies are operating in the neighborhood without permits or oversight?
Are residents reporting safety hazards, sidewalk obstruction, or illegal parking of scooters?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Street Vending Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints exploded to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—indicating either a crackdown by city agencies or a sudden surge in unlicensed vending operations in the district.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69, second-highest anomaly in dataset
This is the most recent spike signal, appearing within current week
reporting_angles: Is the NYPD or Department of Consumer Affairs conducting a targeted enforcement operation in the district?
Are residents complaining about illegal street vendors, or are vendors being cited for violations?

themes_detail.label: Homelessness Encampment Emergence
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 3 last week from a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.42)—signaling a visible and persistent homeless presence in Throgs Neck/Co-op City over the past 1–2 weeks.
evidence: 3 encampment complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
Z-score of 5.42, indicating statistically severe deviation
Spike is recent (last week) and shows emerging homelessness issue
reporting_angles: Where are encampments located, and what triggered their appearance now?
Are there underlying factors—lack of shelter beds, transit hub proximity, or service gaps—driving this?

themes_detail.label: Unlicensed Cannabis Retail Operations
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis Retailer complaints increased to 4 last week from a baseline of 1.0 per week—a 300% spike (z-score: 4.24)—indicating emergence of unlicensed or illicit cannabis shops in the district.
evidence: 4 cannabis retailer complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% spike)
Suggests rapid, likely illegal retail activity in the neighborhood
reporting_angles: How many unlicensed cannabis shops are operating in Throgs Neck, and where are they located?
Is the Department of Finance or law enforcement aware, and what enforcement action is underway?

themes_detail.label: Residential Construction & Plumbing Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: General Construction/Plumbing and Plumbing complaints combined rose to 17 over 2 weeks ago (14 + 3) from baselines of 5.2 and 0.8 respectively—a sustained 167%–300% increase (z-scores: 2.89 and 2.71)—suggesting either major renovation activity without proper permitting or widespread water/plumbing system failures.
evidence: General Construction/Plumbing: 14 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.2 weekly average (167% spike, z-score: 2.89)
Plumbing: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 2.71)
295 total DOB permits filed in last 90 days (206 alterations), suggesting active construction environment
reporting_angles: Are major renovation projects underway at Co-op City or other large residential buildings causing water disruptions?
Are permits being properly filed and inspected, or is unpermitted work driving complaints?
